text.p: Prestigious German camera maker Leica Camera AG said Thursday its net profit for the first half of 1996 rose to 1.9 million marks ($1.3 million) from a loss in the 1995 period despite a meagre gain in sales.
Leica, which issued shares to the public in September, said sales rose 2 percent to 98.5 million marks ($65 million) from 96.5 million marks ($64 million) in the year-ago period.

"The public share offering, the photokina trade fair and also the introduction of two new products made the first half of 1996 a extraordinary turbulent period," Leica management board chairman Klaus-Dieter Hofmann said in a statement.
Despite weak consumer spending conditions in Germany and neighbouring countries, Hofmann said Leica still expected profits and strong sales growth in the second half of 1996.
